extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, project applicants, stakeholders, and persons interacting with the San Francisco Department of Public Works and its Commission
extracted.subtask_short: engaging with SF Public Works Commission
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, rights, and procedural requirements for public participation, disclosure, lobbying, CEQA appeals, and commissioner training related to the San Francisco Department of Public Works and its Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission establishment and governing charter sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Works Commission is established and described in the City Charter, Sec. 4.141. Sec. 4.100-104 of the City Charter describe the rules and powers of executive branch boards and commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the legal basis for the Commission and points to the sections of the City Charter that set out the Commission's establishment, rules, and powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunshine Ordinance — public right to open deliberations
rubrics_metrics.description: Government's duty is to serve the public, reaching its decisions in full view of the public. Commissions, boards, councils and other agencies of the City and County exist to conduct the people's business. This ordinance assures that deliberations are conducted before the people and that City operations are open to the people's review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains citizens' rights under the Sunshine Ordinance (Chapter 67 of the San Francisco Administrative Code) and provides contact information to report violations: Sunshine Ordinance Task Force, City Hall, Room 409; phone (415) 554-7724; fax (415) 554-7854; e-mail sotf@sfgov.org. Copies of the ordinance may be obtained from the Clerk of the Sunshine Task Force, the San Francisco Library, and www.sfbos.org/sunshine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Policy — public disclosure of submitted personal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal information that is provided in communications to the Department of Public Works is subject to disclosure under the California Public Records Act and the San Francisco Sunshine Ordinance. Personal information provided will not be redacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the public are not required to provide personal identifying information when they communicate with the Department. All written or oral communications that members of the public submit regarding projects or hearings will be made available to all members of the public for inspection and copying; the Department does not redact information. Personal information including names, phone numbers, addresses and similar information that a member of the public elects to submit may appear on the Department’s website or in other public documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: San Francisco Lobbyist Ordinance — registration and reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals and entities that influence or attempt to influence local legislative or administrative action may be required by the San Francisco Lobbyist Ordinance [SF Campaign and Governmental Conduct Code Section 21.00-2.160] to register and report lobbying activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the legal citation and directs persons with questions about registration/reporting to contact the San Francisco Ethics Commission at 25 Van Ness Avenue, Suite 220; phone (415) 252-3100; fax (415) 252-3112; or http://www.sfgov.org/ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEQA appeal rights and timing requirements (Chapter 31)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission’s action on a project constitutes the Approval Action for that project (as defined in S.F. Administrative Code Chapter 31), then the CEQA determination prepared in support of that Approval Action is subject to appeal within the time frame specified in S.F. Administrative Code Section 31.16. This appeal is separate from and in addition to an appeal of an action on a project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically, an appeal must be filed within 30 calendar days of the Approval Action for a project that has received an exemption or negative declaration pursuant to CEQA. For filing information contact the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors at City Hall, Room 244, or call (415) 554-5184. If the Department’s Environmental Review Officer has deemed a project exempt, an exemption determination has been prepared and can be obtained online. Important preservation rule: under CEQA, in a later court challenge a litigant may be limited to raising only those issues previously raised at a hearing on the project or in written correspondence delivered to the Board of Supervisors, Planning Commission, Planning Department or other City board, commission or department at, or prior to, such hearing, or as part of the appeal hearing process on the CEQA decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit Bias Training requirement for commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Works Commissioners completed Implicit Bias Training as required by the City and County of San Francisco’s Administrative Code 16.9-28.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records of completion dates are noted (completion dates forthcoming). Signals a statutory training requirement for commissioners; no additional procedural guidance provided on the page.
